newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya rulers, opposition trade blame on violence.
newsitem.headline: Kenya rulers, opposition trade blame on violence.

text.p: Kenya's government and opposition are blaming each other for violence on the Indian Ocean coast that has left 37 dead ahead of a general election this year.
One senior legal expert, while agreeing that politics underpinned the violence, said police treatment of suspects would provide clues to which side was responsible.

"It is pure political thuggery and if it is allowed to go on it will bring down Mombasa which is very much tourist-centred," said Gikandi Ngubuini, a Mombasa lawyer and the chairman of the Law Society of Kenya Coast.

"Political will is an issue here. No person will be taken to court and charged with any offence as high as murder, treason or robbery with violence unless the law enforcement machinery is clearly told to get to the bottom of this," Ngubuini said on Tuesday

Seven days of violence on the coast, centre of Kenya's top foreign currency earner tourism, have shaken the country where President Daniel arap Moi, 73 and in power since 1978, faces elections later this year.
No date has been set for the elections, which threaten to bring more violence.
Two people were killed on Tuesday, bringing the toll in the coastal region to at least 37 dead including police officers. Most civilian casualties were Kenyans not native to the coastal region.
The National Council of Churches of Kenya said it would hold a funeral service on Wednesday at Mombasa Memorial Cathedral for victims.

The violence, which has further tarnished Kenya's international image, comes hard on the heels of protests by an opposition-backed group pressing for constitutional reform that have left at least 12 dead after clashes with police.
An estimated 375 curio stalls were burned at Malindi, north of Mombasa, on Tuesday in the first attack on a tourist site.

"This was the start of the high season and what we make now helps us through the hard times later," said Joyce Atima, who cried as she picked up stone chess pieces from what was left of her Malindi stall.
No tourists have been hurt but foreigners have been told by their governments to avoid troublespots and the United States has warned Americans against going to the coast.
Police have so far arrested 189 people and questioned activists from the ruling Kenya African National Union (KANU) party and opposition groups.
Police spokesman Peter Kimanthi said police were seeking Omar Masumbuko, self-styled chairman of Coast Youth for KANU for questioning.
Moi, speaking in Nairobi, said the country had been "pushed to the wall" and blamed the opposition and reform leaders for creating chaos.
KANU ruled out dialogue with the pro-reform National Convention Executive Committee (NCEC), arguing it used unconstitutional methods to pursue its agenda.
The NCEC called for rallies on August 23 and blamed Moi's advisers for stoking violence on the coast.
